messages:
maria: quick sync 1: we need a pragmatic path to let API keys express per-route RBAC without breaking perf or forcing customers to rotate immediately. thinking: edge translator that mints short-lived scoped leases.

jordan: clarifying Q 1: leases minted by auth-proxy as JWTs? or opaque tokens that require introspection?

maria: prefer JWT-like signed leases for stateless enforcement at runtime. include org/project claims to avoid per-request DB hits. TTL short (1-3m) to limit blast radius.

kevin: perf concern 1: minting on every request is expensive. how do we avoid latency spikes?

maria: propose a prefix cache keyed by (legacy_key, route_template) that serves common patterns. fallback path mints a lease. cache TTL plus pub/sub invalidation on revoke.

security-bot: FYI audit: long-lived keys still ~40% of traffic. revocation currently ~5m to propagate in infra. :warning:

jordan: revocation model? if leases are stateless JWTs we need a way to invalidate immediately when a key is revoked.

maria: combine short TTL + invalidation topic. edge keeps small in-memory blacklist for immediate purge; otherwise rely on TTL window. For sensitive customers we offer introspect endpoint (stateful) for instant revocation.

kevin: signing backend: HSM vs local KMS? HSM adds latency per-sign. batching sign ops or using local KMS with proper key rotation seems better.
jordan: agree. ECDSA P-256 signed JWTs from KMS worker pool; rotate keys and publish key id in token header.

maria: RBAC model notes to include in RFC:
- minimal-claims: route-scoped role set (avoid per-resource claim explosion)
- encode org_id & project_id in token for stateless checks
- opt-in translation per org so migration is safe
- operator API to revoke legacy key and optionally invalidate outstanding leases

devops: ops concerns 1: caches and pub/sub increase edge complexity. also memory pressure from blacklist if many revocations.

maria: mitigations: TTL ceiling (e.g., 3m) to bound blacklist size, and use bloom-filter-ish approximate purge to reduce memory. for enterprise deals, offer stateful introspection and shorter TTLs.

kevin: internal svc-to-svc traffic (background jobs) will suffer if we rely on per-request minting. suggest "service-bound tokens": long-lived token tied to instance identity + narrow roles. include in RFC as alternate flow.

jordan: also document telemetry: mapping table legacy_key -> active_lease_count, 99p mint latency, cache hit rate, revocation latency. these are essential SLOs.

maria: next steps: jordan will draft RFC skeleton with sections: goals, threat model, token formats, caching & invalidation, migration plan, ops runbook, examples. kevin add perf numbers and sample metrics. i'll prepare example JWT payloads and migration checklist.

jordan: ETA draft Tue EOD. tagging @devops for runbook review when ready. :+1:
